newsitem.title: UK: ICO puts world 96/97 coffee crop up at 96.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: ICO puts world 96/97 coffee crop up at 96.5 mln.

text.p: World coffee production could rise to 96.5 million bags in 1996/97 crop year from 86.2 million in 1995/96, the International Coffee Organization (ICO) said.
It said the estimated 12 percent rise in production year-on-year was partly due to the recovery in the Brazilian crop following the damage casued by frost and drought in 1994.
In a document tabled to the week-long ICO meetings this week, the ICO put 1996/97 exportable crop at 72.7 million, up by 11 million from the previous year.

The share of robustas in world exportable production is expected to rise to 30.46 percent in 1996/97 from 26.89 percent a year earlier while the share of arabicas could fall to 69.54 percent from 73.11 percent in the same period.
The ICO said world output could fall in 1997/98 if crop forecasts by Brazilian government sources proved correct.
Estimates from the Brazilian sources indicate the 1997/98 crop would reach between 20 and 22 million bags compared with an estimated crop of 25 million in 1995/96, the ICO report said.
The ICO also said world consumption was estimated at 74.7 million bags in calendar 1996, little changed from 74.9 million in 1995 and 75.3 million in 1994.
But this average was still lower than its 1993 level of 77.0 million.
The ICO said consumption had increased slightly in Europe but has declined in the United States and Japan.
The slight increase in consumption in 1996 was attributable to Europe, particularly the European Union and the central and east European countries.
Stocks of green coffee in main importing nations, including reserves held in free ports, were estimated at 7.0 million bags in December 1996.
Stocks at the beginning of 1997 were equivalent to about four weeks of consumption in the countries in which they were held, the ICO said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
